title: Teaching himself, Floyd Casey's lessons and a homemade first band
summary: He taught himself clarinet and drums, took lessons from drummer Floyd Casey, and recalls making homemade drums with his brother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: When you started, did you have any feature on clarinet or pick it up yourself?

I picked it up myself. I picked it up myself. I picked it up myself. Now on drum, I picked it up myself, but there's a fellow by the name of Floyd Casey. He came down here with no Faith Marvelous, with Faith Marvel. It was him and Floyd Casey and he was a wonderful drummer too.
That's the same guy who used to work with Dewey Jackson? Might have been.

I know he's from way around St. Louis. Yeah, well they played on St. Louis. Yeah, he had a four octave I think of Viperphone. No, he wasn't a Viperphone, remember. Yeah. And then he could play piano too. He was a wonderful drummer. Well I took some lessons for him. But see, after he, I was a fellow to advance fast. I took lessons on the clarinet too, but a fellow wanted to take me away from him because I, I used to, that sit out, you see the method to make the clarinet now, is very simplified. You notice all the youngsters in the school now holding the clarinet down? Oh man, it's beautiful. She's supposed to hold the clarinet on a 45 degree. Some of them hold them, some of them jump on that. For all the schools, all the professors want the money, they ain't giving the real heart of holding the clarinet. And that's important. See, because some of them have some good tones, and I put a nice tone to the clarinet. But I always got that idea from Bechet and them fellas, you know. Well tell us about Sidney Bechet. Yeah, now Sidney Bechet, now let me tell you about that. He used to play a flute, what they call a fife. And my brother had a comb and some of this old brown, thin brown paper. And I went around the market and I got, you know cheese bars, some old cheese bars? Well I went and got some meat off the round steak, that skin, and made drums. And we used to play, a fellow by the name of John, his daddy had a coffin shop. He had a coffin shop, we used to go in there and rehearse him. And they said, I don't know, somehow or another, they wanted to give him a Christmas present. And the first client that they gave him was a Christmas present, I'll never forget that. That looked like that stays in my mind, you know. You know the word, what I'm telling you about is just like a picture. D dear
